meta.label: Code hosting provider
meta.description: How agentflow finds the code host: detected from the Git remotes, or set to a specific forge. A running AI session keeps its old provider until it restarts.

meta.label: Task provider
meta.description: Where tasks live: Jira, GitHub Issues, Asana, or files. None turns task actions off. A running AI session keeps its old provider until it restarts.

meta.label: Knowledge provider
meta.description: Where documents are searched and published: Confluence, a GitHub wiki, or files. None turns knowledge actions off. A running AI session keeps its old provider until it restarts.

meta.label: Checks provider
meta.description: Where CI check results are read from. A running AI session keeps its old provider until it restarts.

meta.label: Deployments provider
meta.description: Where deployment status is read from: GitHub, or a fixture file. A running AI session keeps its old provider until it restarts.

meta.label: Releases provider
meta.description: Where published releases are read from: GitHub, or a fixture file. A running AI session keeps its old provider until it restarts.

meta.label: SecOps provider
meta.description: Where security findings come from for triage. A running AI session keeps its old provider until it restarts.

meta.label: Notification provider
meta.description: How agentflow sends notifications: Slack, a webhook, or a router that sends each signal to several destinations. A running AI session keeps its old provider until it restarts.

meta.label: Self-hosted forges
meta.description: Maps the hostname of a self-hosted code host to its forge type, so agentflow recognises remotes on that host.

meta.label: Self-hosted forges
meta.description: Maps the hostname of a self-hosted code host to its forge type, so agentflow recognises remotes on that host.

meta.label: Source remote
meta.description: Git remote that holds your branches. Without one, agentflow detects it.

meta.label: Source remote
meta.description: Git remote that holds your branches. Without one, agentflow detects it.

meta.label: Target remote
meta.description: Git remote that pull requests go to. Without one, agentflow detects it.

meta.label: Target remote
meta.description: Git remote that pull requests go to. Without one, agentflow detects it.

meta.label: Default project
meta.description: Asana project that bare task IDs and new tasks use, as its GID.

meta.label: Section transitions
meta.description: Maps each Asana project GID to its events and the section GID, completed, or none that each event moves a task to.

meta.label: Site
meta.description: Web address of the Jira site.

meta.label: Projects
meta.description: Jira project keys that My Work and task search look in.

meta.label: Repository
meta.description: GitHub repository, as owner/name, that holds the issues. Without one, agentflow uses the detected code host repository.

meta.label: Labels
meta.description: Labels that agentflow adds to the issues it creates.

meta.label: Open issues only
meta.description: Task search lists open issues only.

meta.label: Search limit
meta.description: Most issues one search returns. Zero uses the default.

meta.label: Task directory
meta.description: Directory in the repository that holds the task files.

meta.label: Repository
meta.description: GitHub repository, as owner/name, that holds the task files. Without one, agentflow uses the current repository.

meta.label: Branch
meta.description: Branch that holds the task files. Without one, agentflow uses the repository's default branch.

meta.label: Task directory
meta.description: Directory in that repository that holds the task files.

meta.label: Publication
meta.description: How task file changes reach the branch: through a pull request, or by pushing.

meta.label: Scope
meta.description: Scope that tasks belong to when a command names none.

meta.label: Scope
meta.description: Scope that tasks belong to when a command names none.

meta.label: Event transitions
meta.description: Maps events and commit verbs to the state a task moves to: open, closed, or none to leave it alone.

meta.label: Event transitions
meta.description: Maps events and commit verbs to the state a task moves to: open, closed, or none to leave it alone.

meta.label: Event transitions
meta.description: Maps events and commit verbs to the state a task moves to: open, closed, or none to leave it alone.

meta.label: Template catalog
meta.description: JSON file in the repository that lists the task templates. Required when task templates are used.

meta.label: Default template
meta.description: Name of the template that new tasks use when none is named.

meta.label: Default template revision
meta.description: Exact revision of the default template.

meta.label: Site
meta.description: Web address of the Confluence site.

meta.label: Publish spaces
meta.description: Confluence space keys that documents may be published to.

meta.label: Repository
meta.description: GitHub repository, as owner/name, whose wiki holds the documents. Without one, agentflow uses the detected code host repository.

meta.label: Document directory
meta.description: Directory in the repository that holds the documents.

meta.label: Repository
meta.description: GitHub repository, as owner/name, that holds the documents. Without one, agentflow uses the current repository.

meta.label: Branch
meta.description: Branch that holds the documents. Without one, agentflow uses the repository's default branch.

meta.label: Document directory
meta.description: Directory in that repository that holds the documents.

meta.label: Publication
meta.description: How new documents reach the branch: through a pull request, or by pushing.

meta.label: Document format
meta.description: Encoding of newly published documents: the open knowledge format, or the legacy format.

meta.label: Document format
meta.description: Encoding of newly published documents: the open knowledge format, or the legacy format.

meta.label: Repository
meta.description: GitHub repository, as owner/name, to read check results from. Without one, agentflow uses the detected code host repository.

meta.label: Repository
meta.description: GitHub repository, as owner/name, to read deployments from. Without one, agentflow uses the detected code host repository.

meta.label: Fixture file
meta.description: JSON file in the repository that stands in for the service, so deployments can be read without credentials.

meta.label: Repository
meta.description: GitHub repository, as owner/name, to read releases from. Without one, agentflow uses the detected code host repository.

meta.label: Fixture file
meta.description: JSON file in the repository that stands in for the service, so releases can be read without credentials.

meta.label: Repository
meta.description: GitHub repository, as owner/name, whose findings agentflow reads. Without one, agentflow uses the detected code host repository.

meta.label: Finding sources
meta.description: Which GitHub alerts agentflow reads: Dependabot alerts, code scanning alerts, or both. An empty list reads none.

meta.label: Minimum severity
meta.description: Lowest severity of a finding that agentflow reports.

meta.label: Incident fixture
meta.description: JSON file in the repository that lists incidents, for triage without a service.

meta.label: Incident scope
meta.description: Stable name for the source of the incident fixture. Required with a fixture.

meta.label: Destination name
meta.description: Name that identifies this destination in delivery receipts.

meta.label: Destination name
meta.description: Name that identifies this destination in delivery receipts.

meta.label: Webhook credential
meta.description: Name of the environment variable that holds the webhook URL. The URL itself never goes in the configuration.

meta.label: Webhook credential
meta.description: Name of the environment variable that holds the webhook URL. The URL itself never goes in the configuration.

meta.label: MCP server
meta.description: Name of the Slack MCP registration used for native delivery.

meta.label: Workspace ID
meta.description: ID of the Slack workspace to send to.

meta.label: Conversation ID
meta.description: ID of the Slack channel or conversation to send to.

meta.label: Required sender
meta.description: ID of the Slack user who must be signed in for delivery. Without one, any signed-in user may send.

meta.label: Header variables
meta.description: Maps an HTTP header name to the environment variable that holds its value.

meta.label: Safe rejection codes
meta.description: HTTP 4xx status codes, other than 408, that guarantee the receiver rejected the request. Only list codes for which a retry is safe.

meta.label: Destinations
meta.description: Named places the router can deliver to. Each has a provider and either a credential or a native Slack scope.

credential_ref.label: Credential
credential_ref.description: Name of the environment variable that holds the webhook URL.

header_refs.label: Header variables
header_refs.description: Maps an HTTP header name to the environment variable that holds its value.

native.actor_id.label: Required sender
native.actor_id.description: ID of the Slack user who must be signed in for delivery.

native.channel_id.label: Conversation ID
native.channel_id.description: ID of the Slack channel or conversation to send to.

native.server.label: MCP server
native.server.description: Name of the Slack MCP registration used for native delivery.

native.workspace_id.label: Workspace ID
native.workspace_id.description: ID of the Slack workspace to send to.

rejected_statuses.label: Safe rejection codes
rejected_statuses.description: HTTP 4xx status codes, other than 408, that guarantee the receiver rejected the request.

meta.label: Routes
meta.description: Maps each signal to the destination names that receive it, in delivery order. Without routes, every signal goes to every destination.

meta.label: Local actions
meta.description: Highest autonomy for local actions such as commit, in every repository.

meta.label: Remote actions
meta.description: Highest autonomy for remote actions such as push and opening a pull request, in every repository.

meta.label: Action overrides
meta.description: Sets the autonomy level for single actions. An override replaces the local or remote level for that action.

meta.label: Approval window
meta.description: How long a confirmation stays valid after agentflow shows its summary. A repository maximum can shorten it.

meta.label: Local actions ceiling
meta.description: Highest autonomy anyone may use for local actions in this repository. A personal level above it has no effect.

meta.label: Remote actions ceiling
meta.description: Highest autonomy anyone may use for remote actions in this repository. A personal level above it has no effect.

meta.label: Action ceilings
meta.description: Caps the autonomy level for single actions in this repository, below the local or remote ceiling.

meta.label: Approval window ceiling
meta.description: Longest time a confirmation may stay valid in this repository. It shortens any longer personal window.

meta.label: Automatic pull request publication
meta.description: Lets an agent open a pull request and push its branch in one step without confirmation, even when the remote ceiling asks for confirmation.

meta.label: Coordinator merge
meta.description: Lets an agent merge a pull request whose base branch is not main or master. The rest of the never-list still applies.

meta.label: Protected branches
meta.description: Branches that changes reach only through a pull request. A pattern with * matches several branches.

meta.label: Test command
meta.description: Command the pull request readiness check runs to confirm that tests pass.

meta.label: Lint command
meta.description: Command the pull request readiness check runs to confirm that lint passes.

meta.label: Commit types
meta.description: Conventional commit types that the commit message check accepts.

meta.label: Subject length
meta.description: Longest commit subject, in characters. Pull request titles stay a little shorter so the squash commit fits.

meta.label: Require a task key
meta.description: Commit subjects must carry a task key, such as a Jira key, that links the commit to its task.

meta.label: Keep AI trailers
meta.description: Keep AI attribution trailers in commit messages. When off, agentflow removes them.

meta.label: Breaking-change paths
meta.description: Path patterns whose changes mark a commit as a breaking change. A pattern may use ** to match any number of directories.

meta.label: Personal worktree root
meta.description: Directory that holds new task worktrees, as root/repository/branch, for repositories that set no root of their own.

meta.label: Primary checkouts
meta.description: Maps a repository name to the directory of its primary checkout, for checkouts outside the default location.

meta.label: Repository worktree root
meta.description: Directory that holds new task worktrees, as root/repository/branch, for everyone who works in this repository.

meta.label: go.work modules
meta.description: Module directories, relative to the worktree root, that the go.work file in each new worktree uses.

meta.label: go.work sibling modules
meta.description: Replaces a Go module in each new worktree's go.work with the same module in another repository: its matching worktree, or its primary checkout.

path.label: Module directory
path.description: Directory of the module inside that repository.

repo.label: Repository
repo.description: Name of the repository that holds the module.

meta.label: Atlassian e-mail
meta.description: E-mail address of your Atlassian account, used to sign in to Jira and Confluence.

meta.label: Jira site
meta.description: Web address of the Jira site. The task provider's own site setting takes precedence.

meta.label: Jira projects
meta.description: Jira project keys the task provider searches. The task provider's own projects setting takes precedence.

meta.label: Confluence site
meta.description: Web address of the Confluence site. Without one, agentflow uses the Jira site.

meta.label: Flow map
meta.description: Where the file is that maps events and commit verbs to Jira statuses: a path in the repository, or owner/repository@ref:path.

meta.label: Update automatically
meta.description: Check for and install new agentflow releases without asking. Turn off to update by hand.

meta.label: Release channel
meta.description: Which releases agentflow offers: stable releases only, or beta releases too.

meta.label: Check interval
meta.description: How often agentflow checks for a new release. An invalid or non-positive value uses the default.

meta.label: Major version
meta.description: Major version of agentflow to follow. Without one, agentflow stays on the installed major version.

meta.label: Pinned version
meta.description: Exact release to stay on. Without one, agentflow follows its channel.

meta.label: Set up new repositories
meta.description: What the AI-client plugins do in a repository that has no agentflow configuration: set it up, only suggest setup, or do nothing. Applies to the listed organisations only.

meta.label: Organisations
meta.description: GitHub owners whose repositories the plugins may set up automatically.
